text:
Marathon Petroleum rose modestly today, continuing a strong four-day rally that has added about $42 per share since early November. The gains reflect tightening conditions in refined products: heating oil prices are up 59% year-over-year heading into winter, and with refineries already running at 95.2% capacity, there's limited room to ramp up production to meet demand. This supply-demand imbalance typically widens the margin refiners earn between the cost of crude oil and the price they get for finished products like diesel and heating oil.

The broader picture, though, is becoming more complex. Russian crude production has rebounded sharply — hitting 8.73 million barrels per day — which the International Energy Agency says has pushed global oil markets back into surplus. A glut of crude supply alongside solid refined-products demand could squeeze refiner margins going forward, which may explain why the stock remains down 6.76% over the past two weeks despite this week's recovery.
